text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London fell to the day's lows in late afternoon trading, as a burst of liquidation and sell stops was prompted by a sell-off in New York. Traders said the weak close could possibly see more selling building-up on Monday as chart patterns were breaking down.

Moreover, the latest beet tests from France and the Russian Federation show very positive results, which points to a good European crop in 1997/98. Moreover, Pakistan may have to sell a lot in 1997/98. October closed $3.10 easier at $320.10 per tonne, while December gave up $1.70 to close at $318.50 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed sharply lower following good sugar beet tests from France and the first beet test results from the Ukraine suggesting crop prospects are much better than last year. However, some traders cautioned that the El Nino global weather pattern may yet reduce supplies.

It was added overall the impact of the El Nino phenomenon is to bring dry weather to Australia and Southeast Asia, resulting in smaller sugar cane crops. Already this season, the Indian crop is about 22 per cent smaller, though India has huge stockpiles of sugar so that the fall had little or no impact on world market prices.

If the European crop should be larger than had been expected, the pressure on prices may hold. October lost 20 points to close at 11.38 cents/lb, while March shed 13 points to close at 11.65 cents/lb.

PAKISTAN - According to the Pakistan Sugar Mills' Association (PSMA) sugar production in fiscal 1997/98 (July/June) is likely to rise sharply to 3 million tonnes, white value. In the 1996/97 season production up to the end of June reached 2.393 million tonnes, compared to 2.470 million tonnes at the same time a year ago and 3.0 million tonnes in 1994/95.

If production should actually reach 3 million tonnes in 1997/98 then the country would have roughly 300,000 tonnes for export as consumption is put at 2.7 million tonnes. By contrast Pakistan imported 596,467 tonnes of white sugar worth $227 million in 1996/97.

RUSSIA - The latest Russian beet test of August 8 showed a sugar content of 10.4 per cent, down from 11.0 per cent at the same time last year, the Rossakhsvyokla, Sugar Beet Producers Association said. The root weight reached 205 grams, up from 178 grams in 1996. This results in a theoretical sugar weight per root of 21.32 grams, nearly 9 per cent up on the previous year's 19.58 grams.

Favourable weather resulted in a speedier root growth which reached 6.3 grams compared to 5.1 grams in 1996. Despite these positive results, sugar production in 1997/98 is still forecast to be lower than last season, due to the lower area sown to sugar beet.

FRANCE - France is apparently heading for a bumper crop. The country's first beet test showed a root weight of nearly 42 tonnes per ha, up from 26.7 tonnes last year and the 1992/96 average of 34.8 tonnes. Sugar content (15.07 per cent) was below last year's level (17.64 per cent) yielding a sugar yield per ha of 6.4 tonnes, white value, up from 4.7 tonnes last year and the average of 5.5 tonnes.

The plant density (105,100 vs 100,900) is also higher than last year. These figures suggest that production this season will be higher than last year, especially as sugar content in the next test must be expected to be noticeably higher, due to the recent dry and sunny weather.
